findings.title: Incorrect type-disjointness check via bitwise AND causes wrong `===` folding in Maglev
findings.message: The `HaveDifferentTypes` / `HasDifferentType` function in the Maglev graph builder uses `IntersectType(lhs_type, rhs_type) == NodeType::kUnknown` (i.e., bitwise AND == 0) to decide that two value-nodes must have different runtime types. This heuristic is semantically incorrect: two NodeTypes can share no bit flags yet still admit a common concrete subtype. The canonical example is `kAnyHeapObject` (bit 5 only, value 32) and `kNumber` (bits 3-1, value 14): their bitwise AND is 0, so the old code declares them disjoint and short-circuits `lhs === rhs` to `false`. However, `kHeapNumber` (= `kAnyHeapObject | kNumber` = 46) is a valid subtype of both, so the same HeapNumber could appear on both sides. When a phi or type-widened node has type `kAnyHeapObject` on one side and a numerically-typed node has type `kNumber` on the other, `BuildTaggedEqual` incorrectly returns the constant `false`, producing a result that diverges from the interpreter and triggers the correctness fuzzer.
findings.suggestion: Replace the bitwise-AND-zero test with a semantic disjointness check. Rather than checking whether the type bits have no overlap (IntersectType == 0), combine the two types with OR (CombineType = bitwise OR) and then test whether the resulting combined type is provably uninhabited according to a curated list of mutually-exclusive property pairs. This is what the fix commit does: it introduces `NodeTypeCannotHaveInstances(CombineType(lhs_type, rhs_type))` with the exclusive-pairs list `{AnyHeapObject,Smi}, {NumberOrOddball,Name}, {NumberOrOddball,JSReceiver}, {JSReceiver,Name}`. Because `CombineType(kAnyHeapObject, kNumber)` equals `kHeapNumber`, which does not appear in any exclusive pair, the two types are correctly recognized as non-disjoint and the `===` fold is not applied.

ground_truth.root_cause: The disjointness predicate confused structural bit-disjointness (no shared flag bits) with logical type-disjointness (no common inhabitant). The NodeType lattice deliberately shares certain bits only along subtype edges, so two types can have no common bits yet share a common concrete subtype (e.g., `kHeapNumber ⊂ kAnyHeapObject` and `kHeapNumber ⊂ kNumber`). Using bitwise AND to test disjointness is only correct when every pair of disjoint concrete types also has disjoint bit representations, which the lattice does not guarantee.
